                       UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                           
6                    WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON                           
                               AT SEATTLE                                     
7                                                                             
     AHP CAPITAL MANAGEMENT LLC,     CASE NO. C25-0007-KKE                    
8                                                                             

                   Plaintiff(s),     ORDER GRANTING MOTION TO                 
9                                                                             
          v.                         WITHDRAW                                 

10                                                                             
     OAK HARBOR CAPITAL LLC, et al.,                                          

11                                                                             
                    Defendant(s).                                             

12                                                                             
         Counsel for Plaintiff filed a joint motion to withdraw representation on August 18, 2025. 
13                                                                             
    Dkt. No. 113.  Counsel served the motion on their client and opposing counsel, and certified that 
14                                                                             
    they informed their clients that business entities such as Plaintiff must be represented by counsel. 
15                                                                             
    Id. at 2.                                                                 
16                                                                             
         Some of the Defendants responded to the motion to request that the Court impose certain 
17                                                                             
    conditions upon the withdrawal.  Dkt. No. 116.  The responding Defendants request that if the 
18                                                                             
    Court grants the motion to withdraw, it should require that (1) the case be stayed for 30 days; (2) 
19                                                                             
    replacement counsel appear no later than 30 days after the order granting the motion to withdraw; 
20                                                                             
    and (3) if replacement counsel does not appear, Plaintiff should be required to show cause why its 
21                                                                             
    claims should not be dismissed for failure to prosecute.  Id. at 2.  Plaintiff did not file a reply brief. 
22                                                                             
         The local rules of this district set out the procedure by which attorneys may withdraw:  
23                                                                             
         No attorney shall withdraw an appearance in any case, civil or criminal, except by 
24        leave of court, unless the withdrawal complies with the requirements of subsections 
1        (b)(2) or (b)(3). … The attorney will ordinarily be permitted to withdraw until sixty 
         days before the discovery cut off date in a civil case, and at the discretion of the 
2        court in a criminal case.                                            

3   Local Rules W.D. Wash. LCR 83.2(b)(1).  Business entities other than sole proprietorships must 
4   be represented by counsel and cannot proceed pro se.  See Rowland v. Cal. Men’s Colony, 506 
5   U.S. 194, 201–02 (1993); see also 28 U.S.C. § 1654; LCR 83.2(b)(4).  If the withdrawing attorney 
6   represents a business entity, “failure to obtain a replacement attorney by the date the withdrawal 
7   is effective may result in the dismissal of the business entity’s claims for failure to prosecute and/or 
8   entry of default against the business entity as to any claims of other parties.”  LCR 83.2(b)(4).  
9   Whether to grant an attorney’s motion to withdraw is committed to the trial court’s discretion.  See 
10   John v. Quality Loan Serv. Corp. of Wash., 857 F. App’x 943, 943 (9th Cir. Sep. 3, 2021).  
11        In this case, Plaintiff’s counsel has complied with the technical requirements of LCR 
12   83.2(b) and the responding Defendants do not oppose withdrawal.  This case is at an early stage 
13   of litigation and no case schedule has been set.  If Plaintiff finds replacement counsel, that 
14   replacement should not result in undue delay to the progress of this litigation.   
15        Accordingly, the Court GRANTS Plaintiff’s counsel’s motion to withdraw, effective 
16   October 16, 2025.  Plaintiff’s outgoing counsel shall email and mail this order to Plaintiff and file 
17   a certificate of service on the docket.  If replacement counsel does not appear by October 16, 2025, 
18   then the Court will order Plaintiff to show cause why its claims should not be dismissed for failure 
19   to prosecute.  All deadlines in this matter are STAYED until further order of the Court. 
20        Dated this 16th day of September, 2025.                              
21                                                                             
                                  A                                           
22                                                                             
                                  Kymberly K. Evanson                         
23                                 United States District Judge                

24
